name: Silverquill Lecturer
oracle_text: Creature spells you cast have demonstrate. (Whenever you cast a creature spell, you may copy it. If you do, choose an opponent to also copy it. Each copy becomes a token.)
blocked_sentences: Creature spells you cast have demonstrate. (Whenever you cast a creature spell, you may copy it. If you do, choose an opponent to also copy it. Each copy becomes a token.)

needs.what: a `controller` (or `players`) field on the `copy_spell` op naming who the copy is put on the stack under the control of -- specifically a player-valued spec such as `{"controller": "chosen_opponent"}` that prompts the source's controller to choose one opponent and creates that opponent's copy under their control, with the chosen opponent then making that copy's own choices (new targets, modes) as its controller
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `op_copy_spell` in src/automtg/engine/effects/ops_stack.py reads only `sid`, `amount` and `new_targets`, and ends `put_copy_on_stack(state, ctx.controller, original, chosen)` -- the copy's controller is hardcoded to the controller of the effect, and `put_copy_on_stack` builds the StackItem with `controller=controller` for that same value. There is no spec key the loader accepts to redirect it (the loader only validates `new_targets` for this op), so every copy this op can make is yours. `for_each_player` does not help: it binds `each_player` into `ctx.bindings` and never reassigns `ctx.controller`, so a `copy_spell` nested inside it still copies under your control. `copy_permanent` does carry a `controller` override, but it copies a permanent already on the battlefield rather than the spell on the stack, so using it would resolve at the wrong time, make the opponent's token a copy of the resolved creature instead of a copy of the spell, and skip the spell copy entirely -- a different card. Dropping the opponent's copy would make the Lecturer a strictly one-sided Cackling Counterpart engine with no downside, which is the half of demonstrate that balances it.
